title: First part only (letters 1..E, E=49-63) under a small-number key (window 5 or 6) on a hidden plain alphabet against A-Z: free key by beam search, period 2-13 keys exactly
k4_result: Exact facts: EASTNORTHEAST fits w=5 (4,288 arrangements), w=6 (36,960). A key repeating with period 2-6 is impossible at w=5 and w=6; period 7 needs w=6 (4 settings), period 8: 7 (w=5) / 18 (w=6), period 9: 0, 10: 84/344, 11: 152/932, 12: 1,072, 13 (block key repeated): 4,288. Part B (period keys, every setting solved by hill climb for E=49 and 63, big model): best K4 reading w=5 -4.613 (p=13, key 1403114102343, NCHSININLETBYTHREDFCWEASTNORTHEASTSTIONTEGOTPLYQU), w=6 -4.806 (p=11, BCFBMAYSEXTACHARGKEYPEASTNORTHEASTNSDUNDANDSWILLP); not English (planted texts reach -4.13 to -4.44). Part A (free key, beam width 2000): best K4 -2.856 (w=5) and -2.669 (w=6) per quadgram, word salad from the pydoc-built model (RMATTHISEDTHESANDEFILEASTNORTHEASTATIONSASSPECIFI).
controls: Shuffled K4s whose first block also fits w<=5 (10 found in seeds 1..2566, 0.39%). Part B w=5: controls -5.027 to -4.593, K4 beats 9/10; w=6: 6 of 10 controls have any period key, -5.407 to -4.759, K4 beats 4/6. Part A with 10 controls: K4 beats 8/10 (w=5) and 10/10 (w=6, -2.669 vs -2.706), so a side check ran 100 more matched controls (seeds 3001-31073): K4 beats 45/100 (w=5, controls up to -2.703) and 88/100 (w=6, up to -2.551). Inside the controls everywhere.
planted: Part B 3/3: period 8 w=5 read back 36/36 unknown letters, rank 1; period 11 w=5 34/36, rank 1; period 7 w=6 true key at rank 2 (a sister setting differing in one key residue scores -4.444 vs -4.490; the true setting reads 28/36). All three beat all 10 controls. Part A 0/3 read back (7-14 of 36-37 letters): the free model fits -2.6 to -2.9, far above the true texts (-4.4 to -4.7). As a score it has power: each plant beats its own matched shuffles 20/20, 16/20, 20/20.
scope_limits: One hidden plain alphabet with cipher letters read on straight A-Z (idea 112's ptX/AZ layout; Vigenere, Beaufort and variant are the same problem there). Key values in a window of 5 or 6 (digits 0-4/0-5 up to a shift); wider windows (digits 0-9) are not tested. Regime 1 is letters 1..E with E=49-63 for the free key, E=49 and 63 for periodic keys. Periods 2-13 at w=5, 2-11 at w=6 (w=6 periods 12 and 13, 7,392 and 36,960 settings, were cut for time). The free-key beam cannot read a planted text back: the model is too loose (about 2.3 bits of freedom per letter), so Part A is a score comparison only, with modest power. No transposition; nothing about the second part's system. Periodic readings are hill-climbed (16 restarts on the top 12 settings per period), not proven optimal.

negative.family: first-part-only small-shift key on a hidden plain alphabet
negative.hypothesis: Letters 1..E of K4 (E before BERLINCLOCK) were enciphered with a key of small numbers (0-4 or 0-5) on a hidden mixed plain alphabet against A-Z cipher letters, which is why EASTNORTHEAST alone fits a window of 5.
negative.scope: ptX/AZ layout, window 5 and 6. Free key: beam width 2000 on the big quadgram model over letters 1-21 and 35-E, E=49-63, alphabet kept exactly as letter domains plus a matching. Periodic key, period 2-13 (w=5) / 2-11 (w=6): every setting the clue block allows, solved by hill climb for E=49 and 63. 10 shuffled K4s with the same w=5 first block (plus 100 more for the free-key score).
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: periods 2-6 impossible at w=5 and 6, period 9 impossible; best periodic reading -4.61 (w=5) / -4.81 (w=6), not English and inside the matched controls (K4 beats 9/10 and 4/6); free-key beam score inside 100 matched controls (45/100 at w=5, 88/100 at w=6), readings word salad (planted periodic 3/3 recovered, 2 at rank 1 and 1 at rank 2; planted free-key texts beat their own shuffles 56/60 but are not read back).

follow_ups: Run periods 12 and 13 at w=6 (44,352 settings, about 30 core-minutes per text) to close the last periodic cells.

The free small-shift key is too loose to read with quadgrams alone. It becomes testable only with a key rule (digits of a date or coordinates, clock readings, a running-number text). Feed candidate digit strings from docs/CLUES.md through the exact periodic/stream path in kryptos/idea133_beam.py.
